newsitem.title: USA: WSCC to okay 6,250 MW intertie rate through June.
newsitem.headline: WSCC to okay 6,250 MW intertie rate through June.

text.p: The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) expects to approve continuing the Pacific Intertie rating of 6,250 megawatts (MW) through the end of June, the WSCC said Wednesday.
The council was awaiting several late votes, but votes received so far, representing a majority, were in favor of the extension, a WSCC spokeswoman said.

Capacity on the 7,900 MW intertie system, which runs from the Northwest to Southern California, was raised to 6,250 MW in late March after being cut to 5,200 MW last summer when the West was hit by two widespread power blackouts.

A technical study group convened by the WSCC is still working on a plan to allow a further increase in the lines' capacity during the spring, but a final plan is not expected until late this month or early May.
The extension approved today will allow the lines to remain at 6,250 MW until June 30 or approval of a spring operating plan or until the onset of summer conditions.
